injuries.note: Left Adelaide’s NBL27 opener against Melbourne United at John Cain Arena on Saturday 19 September 2026 with an ankle injury, reported by basketball.com.au. He started the game. Michael Randall reported on 23 September that Cameron will not fly to Perth for the trip to the Wildcats. Jai at Fox Sports (@NBLPleb) reported on 27 September that Cameron is sidelined in a moon boot on his right ankle and is expected to be out for up to six weeks. That is an upper bound rather than a date, and no starting point was given for it. The NBL’s 29 September update puts his return at Round 5.

Ruled out of the NBL27 season opener against Melbourne United on Saturday 19 September. Adelaide 36ers confirmed it on 18 September: head coach Trevor Gleeson said Humphries "had some ongoing knee injuries" and he did not travel with the squad. Gleeson said he hoped Humphries would be available for the trip to Perth on Thursday, while adding that the club would "just worry about this week". No return date has been given and this is an absence from one game, not a season.
Cairns say scans showed minor ligament damage and put him at 6-8 weeks, with the club aiming to have him back in the early part of the season. The NBL’s 29 September update now lists him as a test.

Blanchfield has a broken finger. Illawarra head coach Justin Tatum, as reported by basketball.com.au on Monday 28 September 2026: “As of right now, I know Todd Blanchfield’s finger is broken. The timeframe is to be determined.” An earlier report, on Sunday 27 September, had described it as a broken thumb with a four-to-six-week absence; the coach has since said no timeframe is set.

Out for Illawarra with a foot injury and awaiting a scan. Illawarra head coach Justin Tatum, as reported by basketball.com.au on Monday 28 September 2026: “Mason will get a scan tomorrow, and hopefully his foot isn’t broken.” No return date has been given. Peatling had left Illawarra’s NBL27 Round 1 game against the New Zealand Breakers at Spark Arena on Sunday 20 September with a back issue; head coach Justin Tatum cleared him the same day, saying “He’s fine. He just got hit on a check-down. He bounced right back and said he’s fine.” That was a back complaint; this one is his foot.

Out of the NBL27 opener against Adelaide on Saturday 19 September, reported by ESPN’s Olgun Uluc on 18 September. Sustained in game two of the Blitz; he did not practice on 8 September and was in the building. No return date has been given. Ili sustained four separate hamstring injuries over the course of last NBL season.

Melbourne United have confirmed the graft from his August 2025 reconstruction failed under rehab loading. He is having a second ACL reconstruction, 9-12 months, and is targeting a return for NBL28 pre-season.

The NBL removed Le Gassick from its own injury list in the 26 September 2026 refresh, having listed him with an ankle injury and no return date. He did not dress for the New Zealand Breakers against Perth at RAC Arena on Friday 26 September. basketball.com.au is holding him as unavailable on that basis; no club or league statement has cleared him.

The Breakers say James has a torn left hamstring and will miss the start of NBL27, and that he will be reassessed in four to six weeks. The club has since signed Mojave King as an injury replacement player, reported by the NBL on September 16, 2026. Reported by Olgun Uluc; the club has not posted it itself.

Not playing against South East Melbourne at RAC Arena on Friday 2 October, confirmed by basketball.com.au. He has now arrived in Perth, after missing the start of the season because he was not yet in Australia. He is not carrying a reported injury. The NBL’s own list carries him as unavailable with the return TBC.

Perth confirmed on 1 October that he is out with a calf injury, will miss Friday’s home game against South East Melbourne and will be re-evaluated in about three weeks. Development player Tana Kopa replaces him on the roster. He left Perth’s 97-93 win over the New Zealand Breakers on 26 September after 7 minutes and 38 seconds, first reported by basketball.com.au that night.

Perth have confirmed a successful reconstruction of a torn ACL in his right knee and say he is expected to miss the entirety of the 2026-27 season. He is a development player, announced by the club on 9 June 2026, and is not in our 12-man projected Perth depth chart. The NBL added him to its own list in the 21 September 2026 refresh.

WIN News Tasmania’s Brent Costelloe reported from the JackJumpers press conference on Wednesday 17 September that Ayre was "still a few weeks away from returning". The NBL’s 21 September list now gives him a return of Round 3, which is consistent with that report. Michael Randall reported on 22 September that he remains out for Tasmania’s trip to Cairns on 23 September.

Michael Randall reported on 22 September 2026 that Deng will miss Tasmania’s trip to the Cairns Taipans on Wednesday 23 September, joining Josh Bannan, Anthony Drmic, Ben Ayre and Bryce Hamilton on the sidelines, without specifying an injury. The NBL’s own list added him as a lower leg injury in its 26 September update, and its 29 September update puts his return at Round 8-10. He did not dress against Cairns.
Tasmania have confirmed the knee injury is an ACL, and have signed Nick Stoddart as a Nominated Replacement Player to cover him for the Blitz and the start of the season.
